topics.title: How to Debug Auto-Debit Failures
topics.content: Auto-debits run on ECS via the `payment-service` worker (triggered by EventBridge). The user API only handles the state and reminders.
topics.resolution: Action: If an expected auto-debit didn't occur, check the `payment-service` logs and the EventBridge execution history first, before assuming the user API failed.

topics.title: Handling Grace Periods & Missed Payments
topics.content: Missed debits trigger a grace period. The user API increments `missedPaymentsCount` and may recalculate monthly targets based on the goal timeline.
topics.resolution: Action: Before manually overriding a missed payment, inspect the goal's `nextDueDate`, `missedPaymentsCount`, and verify if `autoDebitEnabled` is true.

topics.title: Managing the Drop Protocol
topics.content: When a user falls critically behind on funding, the Drop Protocol detaches their savings goal from the travel package and marks it DROPPED, preserving their saved funds.
topics.resolution: Action: If a user was dropped unexpectedly, review their funding percentage and `missedPaymentsCount`. Do not re-link them to a package without resolving the underlying payment failure.

topics.title: Differentiating Reminders vs. Debits
topics.content: Reminders are notifications triggered via a system task; debits are actual payment attempts. A successful reminder does not mean a debit succeeded.
topics.resolution: Action: When handling a complaint, investigate the reminder logs and the payment gateway logs as two completely separate workflows.

topics.title: Reconciling Manual Payment Drift
topics.content: Sometimes a gateway succeeds but the webhook fails, leaving the UfitGo ledger un-updated.
topics.resolution: Action: Always verify the transaction status on the payment gateway dashboard first. Only apply manual credits after confirming the gateway reference and ensuring no duplicate webhooks are pending.

topics.title: Monitoring Booking Progression
topics.content: The Journey Tracker is your dashboard for tracking concierge bottlenecks and documentation readiness. It is NOT the source of truth for payments.
topics.resolution: Action: Use the Tracker to push bookings forward, but escalate payment discrepancies to the finance team instead of forcing status changes in the UI.

topics.title: Advancing Journey Stages
topics.content: Bookings move from checkout -> concierge -> verification -> payment -> fulfilment. Admins should only intervene for exception handling.
topics.resolution: Action: If a booking is stuck, inspect its uploaded documents and operator action history before manually advancing the stage.

topics.title: How to Apply Surcharges
topics.content: Surcharges (for FX changes or operator fees) directly affect the user's financial balance.
topics.resolution: Action: Only apply a surcharge after validating the commercial reason. Confirm that the user received the surcharge notification and their booking amount was updated.

topics.title: Handling Operator Package Disruption
topics.content: If an operator cancels a package, affected users must be migrated without losing their savings progress.
topics.resolution: Action: Coordinate migrations with the finance and operator teams. Do not simply change the `linkedPackageId`—you must also reconcile the booking and payment state.

topics.title: Navigating the Hybrid KYC Model
topics.content: UfitGo uses both legacy KYC fields on the user model and newer KYC profile records. Both affect tier enforcement.
topics.resolution: Action: When investigating a KYC block, check both the legacy KYC status and the new KYC profile table to ensure they align.

topics.title: Monitoring Tier Limits
topics.content: A daily job monitors user balances. If a user approaches 80% of their KYC tier limit, they are flagged for an upgrade.
topics.resolution: Action: If a user complains about limit restrictions, review their current wallet balance against their active tier before approving any large manual withdrawals.

topics.title: Performing Manual KYC Reviews
topics.content: Manual intervention is needed when automated provider checks (e.g., SmileID) fail due to blurry photos or data mismatches.
topics.resolution: Action: Rely on the uploaded user evidence in the Admin Dashboard. If the UI routing seems broken, check the raw verification records directly in the database.

topics.title: Triggering Tier 3 (Address Verification)
topics.content: Tier 3 is requested progressively—only when user balances demand it, or for massive goals like Hajj packages.
topics.resolution: Action: Do not force all new users through Tier 3 verification. Allow the progressive triggers to handle the escalation automatically.

topics.title: Operating the Escrow System
topics.content: Escrow releases funds to operators in tranches based on milestones. Visibility into Escrow is controlled by feature flags.
topics.resolution: Action: If you cannot see the Escrow dashboard, ask an engineer to verify your account's feature flag state before assuming the system is down.

topics.title: Checking Payment Service Health
topics.content: The payment service is strictly versioned under `/api/v1`.
topics.resolution: Action: Use `/api/v1/health` to check if the payment service is online. Do not use legacy `/api/payments` paths.

topics.title: Processing Refunds & Penalties
topics.content: Breaking a savings goal incurs penalties. Refunds must preserve ledger integrity and auditability.
topics.resolution: Action: Before confirming a refund, review the active penalty rules and ensure no pending gateway transactions are in flight.

topics.title: Troubleshooting PTA Batch Failures
topics.content: PTA (Personal Travel Allowance) requests are processed in batches. Failures can occur at the banking layer or internally.
topics.resolution: Action: When a batch fails, isolate the issue: check if the approval failed, the export failed, or the bank submission failed before retrying the batch.

topics.title: Verifying Public Routes
topics.content: Different services handle different API paths on `api.ufitgo.ng` (e.g., `/api/health` vs `/api/v1/*`).
topics.resolution: Action: During an incident, verify the exact URL the frontend is calling. Many "outages" are actually just clients calling deprecated route paths.

topics.title: Triaging Scheduler Incidents
topics.content: Cron jobs are split between ECS EventBridge workers and PostgreSQL-locked in-app tasks.
topics.resolution: Action: For missed tasks, investigate EventBridge for worker jobs, and check the lock tables/logs for in-app jobs. Do not treat all crons the same.

topics.title: Handling Admin UI Route Drift
topics.content: Admin dashboard links occasionally fall out of sync with backend routes during major refactors.
topics.resolution: Action: If a dashboard button 404s, verify if the backend feature was moved behind a feature flag or renamed before escalating a P1 incident.
